The Snot Boogie murder is handled by the homicide squad Bunk Moreland works in as one more routine body, which is exactly the point the scene is making about what the city counts.

Omar Little robbed drug crews for a living and was the most feared man in West Baltimore. The closing sequence of the series shows Michael Lee — a teenager the drug organisation had recruited out of school — holding up a crew with a shotgun in exactly Omar's manner, including his rule that nobody outside the trade is harmed. The series ends by replacing its figures rather than resolving them.

Ellis Carver picks Donut up for stolen cars repeatedly and releases him every time, having no charge that will hold and nowhere to send a boy that age — the arrest becoming a routine the two of them conduct without either expecting it to change anything.

The first case the homicide squad is shown working, in the opening scene of the series. A man who robbed a street dice game every Friday was shot dead, and the witness explains that they let him keep playing because this is America — establishing before anything else that the show is about rules people follow even when the rules destroy them.

William Gant gave truthful evidence at D'Angelo Barksdale's murder trial after the organisation had failed to intimidate or bribe him, and was shot in the back of the head days after the acquittal; D'Angelo, who bore him no grudge, was visibly shaken by the killing.

Omar Little took the stand against Bird Hilton for William Gant's murder — a crime Omar had not witnessed — in payment for what Bird, Wee-Bey and Stinkum had done to Brandon Wright, and the conviction is the one clean result the first season's case produces.
Marcia Donnelly takes Sherrod into Tilghman on the strength of Bubbles's claim to be his uncle, and socially promotes him into a grade far beyond the schooling he has actually had.
Sherrod is placed in Prez's mathematics class and attends exactly once, several grades above the schooling he has actually had, and never returns.

Miss Anna fosters Randy Wagstaff and keeps a household with rules in it; Ellis Carver returns the boy to her after questioning him and tells her he is not a bad kid, an assurance that does not survive the firebombing of her house.

Ellis Carver brings Randy Wagstaff back to Miss Anna after questioning him and tells her the boy is not a bad kid, which is the assurance he cannot make good on once the word snitch reaches the neighbourhood and her house is firebombed.

Randy Wagstaff recruits Donut, Dukie Weems and Kenard to help deliver campaign material on election day, and loses all three when they discover he has already been paid and take their share without finishing the round.

Cheese is Randy's father, a fact David Simon has confirmed and the series never states aloud. A boy being moved between foster placements and a group home has a father a few miles away, prospering in the city-wide drug dealers' association, and neither ever learns of the other.
Proposition Joe is Cheese Wagstaff's uncle and gave him a crew on family grounds, an appointment he spends years absorbing the consequences of and is finally killed by.

Omar Little takes his grandmother Josephine to Sunday mass every week, in the one arrangement he keeps that has nothing to do with robbing anyone, and it is that routine the Barksdale organisation uses to find him.

Two Barksdale soldiers fire on Josephine and Omar Little as they walk to church; she is unhurt but loses her hat, and Avon Barksdale — furious at the breach rather than the attempt — makes the shooters pay for a replacement.
Omar Little observes the Sunday truce like everyone else in the trade, which is precisely why he is walking to church unarmed with his grandmother when the Barksdale soldiers find him.
The Barksdale organisation had kept the Sunday truce for years, and Avon Barksdale's anger at its breach is about the rule rather than about Omar Little surviving.

Stringer Bell gave two soldiers the go-ahead to shoot at Omar Little on a Sunday morning, breaking a rule the whole city had kept; it restarts a war he had been trying to end and leads directly to his own killing.

Avon Barksdale paid Devonne to seduce Marlo Stanfield and lure him to a second meeting where Barksdale soldiers would be waiting, a plan that fails because Marlo sends Chris Partlow to look at the location first.
Marlo Stanfield sleeps with Devonne and then works out what she was for, which in his organisation is the same discovery twice over.
Marlo Stanfield shot Devonne himself rather than send Chris Partlow, one of only two murders he commits personally in the entire series, and had her body left where it would be found.
Louis Sobotka is Nick's father, stayed clear of his brother's arrangement with the Greeks entirely, and is the one who talks Nick into surrendering once the warrant is out.

Louis Sobotka is Frank's elder brother, retired early from the shipwright's trade the port no longer supports, and watched Frank spend the union's money trying to keep the same work alive for the next generation.
Nick Sobotka and Aimee have a daughter, Ashley, and no house to raise her in; the money Nick makes moving the Greeks' product is money for a place of their own.
Josephine raised Omar Little; she is the only family member the series shows him in contact with, his brother Anthony being mentioned and never appearing.
Louis Sobotka is Ziggy's uncle — Frank's elder brother — which makes Ziggy and Nick cousins rather than brothers, the family arrangement the second season keeps being misread as.
Spider beat Dukie Weems on the corner, the assault that prompts Michael Lee to walk Dukie round to Cutty Wise's gym in React Quotes and ask for self-defence training.

Raylene Lee is Michael's mother; her addiction and her readiness to let Bug's father back into the flat are why Michael takes on the household himself and will not discuss it with Prez, Cutty or anyone else.
Raylene Lee is Bug's mother as well as Michael's, and it is her custody that Michael is effectively removing the boy from when he takes over feeding and collecting him from school.

Johnny Weeks's body is found in a vacant house inside the Hamsterdam free zones in Mission Accomplished, dead of an overdose — the experiment's clearest cost shown alongside its falling crime figures.

Maurice Levy defended D'Angelo Barksdale at the murder trial that opens the series, winning an acquittal after the organisation frightened the second witness into recanting — the outcome that sends McNulty to Judge Phelan and creates the detail.
Devar Manigault is Raylene Lee's domestic partner; she allowed his abuse of Michael to continue because she depended on his money, and welcomed him back into the flat on his release.
Devar Manigault is Bug's father, and it is his turning toward the younger boy after his release that makes Michael Lee act rather than simply endure it as he had himself.
Chris Partlow beat Devar Manigault to death in a vacant rather than shooting him as usual, having got the reason out of Michael Lee, and the DNA he left at that scene is what finally convicts him.

Michael Lee accepted Chris Partlow's offer of work and protection on the condition that Devar Manigault — his abuser, and now Bug's — was removed, which is the debt that binds him to the Stanfield organisation.

Crutchfield will not let Bunk reopen the Omar Little murder, because a killing already written up as solved would revert to unsolved on his own record. He threatens to undo one of Bunk's closures in retaliation, and bins a message that would have taken detectives to the boarded-up houses months earlier than they got there.

Vernon Holley agrees, reluctantly, to help Bunk Moreland reopen the Omar Little case, and intimidates Old Face Andre into admitting he helped frame Omar — accepting a hit to his own clearance rate to do it, which is the opposite of what Crutchfield does with the same case.
Vernon Holley took Old Face Andre's identification of Omar Little as a murder suspect, and later broke the same statement down until Andre admitted the framing.

A murder is committed inside the three blocks where Colvin has quietly stopped arrests, and Crutchfield, the detective assigned to it, agrees to sit on the investigation rather than expose the arrangement. Colvin repays him by squeezing the dealers there until a suspect is produced — an easy solved case in exchange for silence.
Cedric Daniels encouraged Leander Sydnor to transfer into the Major Crimes Unit when he was allowed to pick his own detectives, filling one of the places Herc Hauk and Ellis Carver had vacated.

Spider ends the fourth season working for Michael Lee on Bodie Broadus's old corner, and is seen in the final episode running that corner himself — the succession the series shows happening one rung at a time.
Spider becomes a regular at the gym in the fourth season after befriending Justin, and goes back to the corner when Cutty Wise alienates him by sleeping with his mother.
Spider and Sherrod work as dealers together before Spider moves to Monk Metcalf's crew, the two of them being the boys the fourth season shows outside the school storyline entirely.
Spider deals for Monk Metcalf's crew after leaving the gym, one rung of the Stanfield organisation below the men who handle its money and phones.

Jimmy McNulty feeds Scott Templeton as an anonymous source, phoning him in Took through a voice modulator as the invented serial killer and sending a photograph of a homeless man he has staged as a victim; in the finale he tells Templeton to his face that he started the whole thing, knowing the reporter can never repeat it.
After Frank Sobotka is killed the stevedores re-elect him treasurer in defiance of federal warnings — a gesture that costs them the local, which is dissolved as a result.

Kimmy and Tosha Mitchell were partners in both senses — robbing drug dealers together before Omar Little came back to Baltimore, and joining his crew as a pair once he did. Tosha's death is what ends Kimmy's willingness to keep hitting Barksdale stashes.

The Greek is registered as Koutris's informant, which is the arrangement that protects him: in exchange for what he passes on, Koutris seals the file Fitzhugh requests on George Glekas and warns the organisation that the port investigation is closing in.
Koutris works outside the Baltimore field office, which is why Fitzhugh's request about Glekas reaches him at all and why nobody local understands where the leak came from.

Terrance Fitzhugh asks a fellow agent to look into George Glekas and gets a sealed file back; the man he asked is the Greek's handler, and the query itself is what tells the organisation to clear out.

The FBI lends the city investigators surveillance equipment and analysts while making clear that federal resources have moved to terrorism and political corruption, so a municipal drug case is nobody's priority. When the police later ask for real federal help, the offer arrives attached to a corruption investigation into City Hall they cannot accept.

Odell Watkins mentors Marla Daniels through her run for a city council seat, and Clarence Royce — refusing Watkins's demand that Burrell be sacked — tries to buy him off by backing her candidacy instead.

Wallace recognises Brandon Wright from a surveillance photograph and points him out to the Barksdale crew, not understanding what will follow; the tortured body left on the fence afterwards is what breaks Wallace and makes him ask to come off the corner.
Maurice Levy negotiates Monk Metcalf's twenty-year plea as part of the settlement that follows the exposure of the illegal wiretap.
Maurice Levy handles Chris Partlow's case in the same settlement, trading a life sentence for Partlow against Marlo Stanfield walking out of the courthouse free.

Vondas hands Nick Sobotka the serial numbers of the containers to lose from the port computer, meeting him at the diner rather than the docks and moving him from stolen cameras to drugs a step at a time.

Nerese Campbell brokers the terms on which Ervin Burrell leaves the commissioner's office — a quiet exit and a pension in exchange for his silence about what he knows of Cedric Daniels's finances — which is the deal that lets Carcetti replace him without a fight over race.

Stanislaus Valchek gets the commissioner's office from Nerese Campbell, having spent five seasons trading favours toward exactly that end — the man whose grudge over a church window created the second season's investigation ending in command of the department.

Spider trains at Cutty Wise's gym through the fourth season until Cutty sleeps with the boy's mother, after which Spider stops coming and goes back to the corner — the one occasion Cutty's own conduct costs him a boy he had kept off the street.

The State's Attorney's office takes the Clay Davis prosecution out of federal hands and tries it in state court, where Davis talks the jury round and walks out acquitted — the case Lester Freamon's financial work had been built for.
